title: ERD Studio fields
description: The fields this project records: .erd-studio/fields.yml. Two lists, tables and columns, in the order the Detail panel shows them. A bare name is a built-in field exactly as ERD Studio ships it; an entry with a key is a built-in in your own words, or a field of your own. Without this file a project uses the starting set. Reference: https://github.com/liam-machine/erd-studio/blob/main/docs/semantic-domain-json-reference.md#field-list-erd-studiofieldsyml

$schema.description: Optional schema reference for editors outside VS Code. Ignored by ERD Studio.

version.description: The file format version. 1 today; leave it out and it reads as 1.

tables.description: Fields recorded on tables, in display order. Leave the list out to use the starting set's table fields (grain, purpose, decisions, open_questions, role, scd_strategy, measures); an empty list means none.

columns.description: Fields recorded on columns, in display order. Leave the list out to use the starting set's column fields (natural_key, scd_type, additive_type); an empty list means none.

left_out.description: dbt meta: keys that are another tool's settings (Lightdash's dimension or metrics, say): never copied or offered. A table that already has one still shows it.

tableBuiltInName.description: A built-in table field, exactly as ERD Studio ships it.
enumDescriptions: Grain (text). One row per ___. The one sentence that says what a row is.
Purpose (text). Who uses this table and the question it answers.
Decisions (text). A choice a later editor might undo, and why.
Open questions (text). What is still undecided. Assistants ask about these and never guess.
Table role (choice). Which kind of table this is: conformed-dim, transaction-fact, …
History (text, dimensions only). How this dimension keeps history: which columns track changes and which overwrite.
Measures (text, facts only). How the measures add up: which sum across every dimension and which do not.
Source of truth (value, optional). The system this data is mastered in.
Freshness (text, optional). How fresh it must be, and how often it loads.
Known issues (text, optional). Data problems a consumer should know before trusting a number.
Retention (text, optional, people only). How long rows are kept, and why.
Design (retired: still read and shown, never offered). Move to Decisions, or to Purpose.
Role choice (retired: still read and shown, never offered). Move to Decisions.
Grain choice (retired: still read and shown, never offered). Move to Decisions.

columnBuiltInName.description: A built-in column field, exactly as ERD Studio ships it.
enumDescriptions: Natural key (yes-no). The business identifier, like an order number or a customer code.
SCD type (choice 0, 1, 2; dimensions only). 0 never changes, 1 overwrites, 2 keeps history.
Additivity (choice; facts only). Additive, semi-additive or non-additive.
Business rule (text, optional). How the value is worked out, in business terms.

tableKey.description: The setting's name in the table file. Lower case letters, digits and underscores (DBML lower-cases setting names), not starting with a digit, and not a reserved name: DBML's own settings (note, pk, default, …), ERD Studio's (schema, alias, meta_json, …), or anything starting erd_, rationale_ or meta_. A built-in's own key (grain, role, natural_key, …) is allowed: it rewords that built-in.

columnKey.description: The setting's name in the table file. Lower case letters, digits and underscores (DBML lower-cases setting names), not starting with a digit, and not a reserved name: DBML's own settings (note, pk, default, …), ERD Studio's (schema, alias, meta_json, …), or anything starting erd_, rationale_ or meta_. A built-in's own key (grain, role, natural_key, …) is allowed: it rewords that built-in.

tableEntry.description: A built-in table field in your own words (its key plus label, guidance or filled_by), or a table field of your own.

label.description: What the canvas and the assistant call it. Built-ins have one already.

type.description: How it is filled in. A built-in's type cannot be changed (ignored, with a warning).
enumDescriptions: The default. A sentence or two of explanation: a text box, with the guidance as its placeholder.
One short value with no fixed list, like a team or a system name: a one-line box.
One of the field's values: a dropdown. Needs at least two values.
True or false: a yes or no dropdown, written 'true' or 'false'.

values.description: For a choice: the only values allowed, in dropdown order (at least two).

guidance.description: One sentence: what to write. It is the canvas placeholder and the assistant's instruction.

enumDescriptions: The default: people or the AI.
People only: an assistant writes only a value the user gives it.
Copied from the dbt model's meta:, never typed in. With no value in dbt, nothing is written.

show_for.description: Which tables it suits, read from the table's role. A field with a value always shows anyway. A built-in's show_for cannot be changed.
enumDescriptions: The default: every table.
Dimensions: conformed-dim, domain-dim, gold-dim and reference (and tables with no role).
Facts: transaction-fact, periodic-snapshot, accumulating-snapshot, factless-fact and gold-fact (and tables with no role).
